name: Orkes: Create an OpenAI Integration and Model Before Building an LLM Workflow
query: I'm on our Orkes Conductor cluster (CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL=https://acme.orkesconductor.io/api, CONDUCTOR_SERVER_TYPE=Enterprise, and my application key/secret are already in the environment). Build me a workflow that summarizes a support ticket with OpenAI gpt-4o-mini. My OpenAI key is exported in my shell as OPENAI_API_KEY. I don't think OpenAI is set up on the cluster yet.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Recognize the target is Orkes, where LLM providers are cluster integrations (SKILL.md Rule 16, references/orkes-integrations.md) — not server env vars
Step 2: Check what exists first: `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" integration-list --category AI_MODEL` and `model-list --provider <name>`; reuse an existing OpenAI integration if there is one

Step 3: If none, confirm before creating it, then `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" integration-save --name <name> --type openai --config-env api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY` — key read from the env var, never in chat, argv or workflow JSON

Step 4: Register every model the key can use, discovered live: `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" model-sync --provider <name> --type openai --key-env OPENAI_API_KEY` (optionally `--dry-run` first) — gpt-4o-mini included — and use WebSearch/WebFetch on OpenAI's models page to tell the user which models are the latest
Step 5: Note access: the application that created the integration has access automatically; other applications/groups need a grant (UI Access Control or `grant-access`)
Step 6: Write an LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE workflow to a file with `llmProvider` = the integration NAME and `model: gpt-4o-mini`, `messages` using `{role, message}`, and register it
Step 7: Verify with a test execution
success_criteria: Checks existing AI integrations (`integration-list` and/or `model-list`) before creating one

Creates the integration via `integration-save` (or `POST /api/integrations/provider/{name}`) with type `openai`, reading the key from the environment (`--config-env api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY` or equivalent) — the key value never appears in chat, a command argument or the workflow

Registers all models the key can use, discovered live (`model-sync` / `provider-models` against OpenAI's model list, or an equivalent live lookup + `model-save` per model) — not only `gpt-4o-mini` and not a list typed from memory — with `gpt-4o-mini` among them
Looks up online (WebSearch / WebFetch of the provider's models page) which models are current/latest and reports that to the user
The LLM task's `llmProvider` is the integration name that was created or found (not assumed to be the literal type `openai` unless that is the integration's name) and `model` is `gpt-4o-mini`
Addresses access: states the creating application gets access automatically and/or how other applications/groups are granted access
Does not present 'set OPENAI_API_KEY in the server environment' as the Orkes fix, and does not invent a `conductor integration` CLI command
Does not fall back to an HTTP task calling api.openai.com
Workflow JSON is written to a file before registration and the plan includes a verification run
